cells.tense: The work runs at its own pace and you can see its whole shape without wincing at it.
cells.ask: Put one unfinished piece in front of somebody whose eye you trust and ask a single question about it, then stop talking. New eyes on the whole are worth more than another pass alone.
cells.core:
Practice like yours is moving without being shoved, and you can step back from your own work, find the weak joint, and return to it without either defending it or sinking into it. The standing-back and the going-deeper are on the same side now, which is rarer than it feels from inside.

What the steadiness can carry forward is a sharper eye, and a sharper eye comes from somebody else's question rather than more hours alone with the thing. Hand the small piece to the person you'd trust to be honest. Whatever they say will teach you something, right or wrong.
cells.sheetLine: You can see your own work clearly and keep building it anyway.
cells.verb: keeping at the same craft until the depth itself is the breakthrough
cells.place: back far enough to see how the whole thing fits together

cells.tense: You're living several passes beyond where the work actually is.
cells.ask: Do the next small step at its real size today, then tell one person one thing you noticed while doing it. It gives the finished version something on the ground to stand on.
cells.core:
Done well, this is a person who can hold the finished form in mind and still enjoy the rough pass — the eye and the hand pulling in the same direction, no rush in it. That version is available from here.

Where you're standing, everything on the bench reads as beneath the version in your head, so the piece gets redone, rated, measured against a standard it hasn't reached. The comparing crowds out the contact that actually grows a hand, and the mastery you're braced for doesn't arrive this way.

One honest pass, done today, and one person told what it showed you, keeps what you see tied to the ground it's meant to serve.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the work to a version of itself that doesn't exist yet.

cells.tense: You went quiet at some point and haven't come back into the open with it.
cells.ask: Take whatever you're actually making right now and say out loud where it stands, to one person, without dressing it up. Saying it that way keeps the shape visible and puts you back where you can see your own work.
cells.core:
You can still read the whole structure of what this is becoming, and the patience hasn't left you. You hold the shape in your head, and when you say what you see, other people steady themselves on it because it's true. That part is intact.

What stopped is putting any of it where anyone can watch. Judged alone long enough, or unseen long enough, the work goes quiet, and the quiet starts to look like the end of the craft when it isn't.

Where the work honestly is, said to one person, at whatever stage it's at, is a claim you get to hear yourself make. It won't settle everything at once. It ends the silence for one person, and you find out what you think while somebody listens.
cells.sheetLine: The craft is intact. You've just stopped letting anyone see it.

cells.tense: You're the one holding the work together, and you tell it as if it assembles itself.
cells.ask: Pick one moment this week when something landed the way it did because of how you saw it coming — name it as yours right there, then say the same thing to one other person. It hands you the wheel you say you're only riding.
cells.core:
Said plainly, this is someone who can name what they saw and why it mattered, and let others take it or leave it. Reading the whole shape is already happening — where a decision lands three steps out, what the work needs next, what's worth keeping.

Instead you talk as though anyone paying attention would notice the same things. Most wouldn't. That reading is doing the real work of holding this together, and you're the only one treating it like background.

One place where your eye shaped how it went, named as yours, and then said to somebody who wasn't there, gives it back to you. Nothing gets claimed away by being said out loud.

attempts.check: The records give me the card as sustained craft toward mastery and the seat as seeing the whole pattern from inside it, but nothing about this person's trade, training, or audience — so every cell has to stay on the mechanism and leave the life to the person. A reader could reasonably say that 'seeing the pattern is yours' is unfalsifiable flattery, or that a non-reader's pattern-sight looks like ordinary attentiveness; I've kept it as a condition a person can refuse rather than a badge. The asks survive a wrong read — a question asked, a piece shown, a stake named out loud all produce something whether or not the diagnosis is right. The sentence I cut was a tidy line about the work not needing a witness, which was the writer admiring himself.
